newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares plunge 5.07 pct as new govt hopes fade.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares plunge 5.07 pct as new govt hopes fade.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell sharply in strong selling on Tuesday after conservative leader Tansu Ciller refused to discuss a planned secularist pact in talks with prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,684, down 90 points, or 5.07 percent from Monday when it surged 8.04 percent to an all-time high close of 1.774. It was down 3.49 percent at the end of the first session.
Trade volume fell sharply to 34.42 trillion lira from Monday's 45.48 trillion.
Brokers said selling pressure which started as a correction of Monday's steep rise accelerated on political news which sharply reduced the chances of a secularist right-left alliance to be set up.
They said bluechip shares of state owned enterprises and utilities which had gained most during Monday's rally led the way in sales as well.
Bearish sentiment was fuelled by leftist leader Deniz Baykal's remarks that his party would support the new coalition but wanted early elections to be held by the end of 1997.
In the afternoon, conservative True Path Party (DYP) leader and Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller's remarks shook the market.

"I did not discuss the government issue, so as not to legitimise Yilmaz's position... We said to Yilmaz, 'Go immediately and return the mandate to the president,'" Ciller told reporters after 20 minutes of talks with Yilmaz.

Yilmaz is short of simple majority needed in parliament to win a confidence vote even with the support of two left-wing parties, a small grouping which broke away from the DYP and independent conservatives.

"The market is indexed to a forthcoming vote of confidence in a new government. Yesterday's optimism faded after the DYP refused to support Yilmaz's initiative," said Hayri Fevzioglu from Cagdas securities.
President Suleyman Demirel on Friday asked Yilmaz to form a government to end months of political turmoil but Ciller says she should have been nominated for the job.
She said she would offer Yilmaz the chance to join a coalition under her leadership if he failed to cobble together an alliance in the coming days.
Brokers said the market would react positively to developments that would increase the chances of a secularist alliance winning a confidence vote in parliament.

Of the 244 shares traded, falls outdid rises sharply by 217 to 17 and 10 were unchanged. The IMKB Industrial lost 4.35 percent to 1,605, IMKB Services shed 4.4 percent to 1,696 and the IMKB Financial dived 5.55 percent to 1,788.

Leading actives were utilities Cukurova Elektrik, down 7,500 lira at 240,000 and Aktas Elektrik, down 12,500 lira at 232,500, largely state-owned firms -- flat steel maker Eregli, down 750 lira at 23,000, petroleum products marketer Petrol Ofisi, down 2,000 lira at 24,500 and Turkish Airlines, down 4,000 lira at 37,500. They made up 44.7 percent of the total turnover.
